interactions.target_raw: Major histocompatibility complex, class I, B
interactions.note: The antibody phage clones bound to HeLa cells expressing HLA-B*57:01 modified by abacavir  better than to the drug-free HLA-B*57:01. The phage clones also showed a low level of binding to cells expressing HLA-B*57:03 or HLA-B15 allotypes (HLA-B*15:01 or HLA-B*15:02), but could not recognize HLA-B27 or HLA-B35. Critical residues were determined by introducing mutations Met45Thr and  Ala46Glu, which prevented the binding of phage antibodies to HLA-B57 and HLA-B15. Conversely, the phage clones  #1, #2, and #3 acquired binding potential to the artificially mutated HLA-B27 and HLA-B35 following the introduction of Met45 and Ala46 in the heavy chain region. These findings indicated that Met45 and Ala46 in HLA-B57 and HLA-B15 are crucial for the  binding of the selected phage antibodies.

interactions.note: The antibody phage clones bound to HeLa cells expressing HLA-B*57:01 modified by abacavir  better than to the drug-free HLA-B*57:01. The phage clones also showed a low level of binding to cells expressing HLA-B*57:03 or HLA-B15 allotypes (HLA-B*15:01 or HLA-B*15:02), but could not recognize HLA-B27 or HLA-B35. Acidification to elute any components within the peptide binding groove in the HLA-B*57:01 complexes, increased the binding affinity of the phage antibodies, implying that the selected antibodies recognized peptide-deficient HLA-B*57:01.
